description: Jan Evertsenstraat 59-87 odd (1927): plain dark brown brick; per house a French door at the party wall with a stacked concrete balconette on every upper storey and a hood slab over the top one (two houses' slots flank one brick pier), a wide two-light casement under a fixed top light touching the door, and half of a window that straddles the far party wall (the mirrored neighbour completes it); a glass-block band (on 75-87 a painted sign panel) over the continuous rigid canopy; a tall plain parapet (about 3.3 m) with a thin coping

parapet.note: 3.3 m of plain brick over the storeys (13.7-17.0 m on 61)

raised-end.note: a raised stair-tower end at a row end (89 at the Vespuccistraat side is a stepped corner, not drawn)

rhythm.bays: per house, slot side first: the slot pier 0.3 m, the French door 0.93 m touching a wide two-light window 1.88 m, plain wall 1.23 m, and half (1.69 m) of the window that straddles the far party wall
rhythm.identicalBays: every upper storey the same; houses mirror in pairs so two slots flank one pier
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: shop | 1-3: French door + window touching, half a party-wall window
rhythm.symmetry: mirrored pairs about the slot pier
rhythm.groundFloor: shop under the continuous rigid canopy, a glass-block band over it
rhythm.signage: letters on the glass-block band (not drawn)
rhythm.roofline: tall plain parapet with a thin coping
schemaLimits: signs on the glass-block band are not drawn
the two halves of a party-wall window keep a 4 cm brick pier between them (one window on the photo)

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-12-06, ruler crop of 61: canopy fascia 2.55-3.05 m, glass-block band 3.1-4.5 m (1.4 m, 7 rows), wall 4.5-5.4 m (16 courses to the sills), windows 5.4-7.0 / 8.3-9.9 / 11.2-12.85 m (pitch 2.9 m; floors 5.0/7.9/10.8 m give sill 0.14, head 0.69, height 0.55 of the storey), French doors from the floors, balconette slabs about 0.15 m at each floor, the top hood slab about 0.2 m at 13.35-13.6 m, eaves 17.0 m: 3.3 m parapet (60 courses); windows 1.6-1.85 m wide, door 0.6-0.7 m
strip.jpg 2024-12-06 (zoom of 59-63 and the strip at 69, 81): the same slot stacks every other party wall; 81 (110182) hood and slabs as on 61

strip.jpg 2024-12-06, ruler crop (120 px/m) of 61 (slot on its left): the slot pier 0-0.3 m, the French door 0.32-1.23 m touching a 1.88 m two-light window (1.23-3.11 m), plain wall, then 4.34-6.03 m of a window centred on the party wall with 63; the window rows 5.4-7.0 / 8.3-9.9 / 11.1-12.9 m. The slots pair at every other party wall (59|61, 63|65, 67|69 ... 85|85A), as on the hood-lisene rows

palette over the type's 14 pands (de-baarsjes-palettes.ts): wall #54402a, frames #aaaa91, coping/cornice band #4b4131; glass-block rows 3.4-4.2 m #555645 type-wide, #535442 on 61 (3.3-4.4 m); hood slab on 61 #7e7a5f (concrete), balconette slab edge #5d5d48 (in shadow)

notes: Each house's shop gives awning {style: rigid, glassBlocks: {rows: 7}, wallCourses: 16}; palette.band is the hood/slab concrete (the hood slab takes the band colour).

The slot pier is a lisene (leftEnd half): two houses' halves make the 0.4 m pier between their slots, from the band to the parapet. photoRows count columns: the French door and its touching window read as one.
Place with mirror: true on every other house so the slots pair up at the shared pier; the party-wall windows then meet across the other party wall.
On 75-87 the band over the canopy is a painted sign panel: glassBlocks {rows, panel: '#rrggbb'} draws it flat in the measured colour.
